description:
The substrate's own gap-narrowing loop is measurably inert: 259 narrowing operations produced a 0.4 percentage-point change in landing rate.

MEASURED 2026-09-08, PAIRED WITHIN-GAP. For every gap with a corresponding -narrowed variant (259 pairs), comparing the original against the narrowed version of the SAME gap:
  summary contains a concrete proposed change : parent 5%  -> narrowed 8%
  landed (acquired a sha, or closed landed_verified) : parent 7.3% (19/259) -> narrowed 7.7% (20/259)

This is a paired design on the same underlying gap before and after the substrate reprocessed it, so it is free of the selection bias that confounds cross-sectional gap comparisons - notably the confound that dissolved a region-anchor result earlier the same day, where an apparently significant 6.9% vs 1.9% difference turned out to reflect which gaps were well-specified rather than any effect of the intervention.

WHY THIS MATTERS. Narrowing is the substrate's mechanism for improving its own inputs: taking a gap it could not act on and reworking it into something it can. The architecture expects exactly this kind of self-improvement of the work queue. Measured over 259 attempts, it does not produce one. A loop that reprocesses gaps without making them more actionable consumes compose capacity - each narrowed gap is another entry competing for a cap-1 lane - while returning nothing.

THE TWO NUMBERS ARE CONSISTENT WITH EACH OTHER, AND THAT IS THE LEAD. Narrowing barely raises concreteness (5% to 8%) and correspondingly barely raises landing (7.3% to 7.7%). Separately measured across 995 gaps carrying an edit_site, gaps whose summary contains a concrete proposed change land at 28.4% versus 9.6% for gaps that only describe the defect, and that gap survives within-file matching (26.0% vs 8.1% across files containing both kinds, holding directionally in 5 of 6 files). If concreteness is the operative variable, then narrowing fails precisely because it does not supply it: it rewords the description rather than proposing the change.

WHAT TO CHANGE. Narrowing should be judged on whether its output contains a concrete proposed edit - the actual change, anchored on a literal verified to occur exactly once in the deployed file - not on whether the description got shorter or more specific in prose. A narrowed gap that still only describes a defect has not been improved in the dimension that predicts landing.

FALSIFIER. Recompute the paired comparison. The defect is resolved when narrowed gaps land at a materially higher rate than their parents, or when the share of narrowed summaries carrying a concrete proposed change rises well above the current 8%.

ROOT CAUSE FOUND IN CODE (repos/development-vessel/src/resolvers/gap-to-feature.ts, the chronic-failure narrowing branch). At the moment the narrowed child is created it does exactly two things:
  childMeta = { ...meta, failed_attempts: 0, parent_gap_id: parentId, narrowed_at: ... }
  summary   = `[narrowed from ${parentId}] ${parentSummary}`
The summary is the PARENT'S text with a prefix prepended. There is no narrowing step - nothing shortens the description, extracts the failing statement, or proposes a change. The comment directly above the branch nevertheless states "The child carries a tighter description", which the code does not implement. That comment is the specification this code fails to meet.

SO THE ONE RELIABLE EFFECT OF NARROWING IS RESETTING THE FAILURE COUNTER. The code says so itself: failed_attempts is set to 0 "so it re-enters the dispatch queue at normal priority rather than being culled by the landabilityScore filter". That filter exists to deprioritise gaps the substrate has repeatedly failed to land. Narrowing therefore launders chronic failure back into the queue at full priority without changing anything about why the gap kept failing.

CONSISTENT WITH THE MEASUREMENT. 259 narrowing operations, landing 7.3% -> 7.7%, concreteness 5% -> 8%. If the description is carried across unchanged, no landing improvement is expected, and none is observed.

MEASUREMENT CAVEAT, STATED HONESTLY. Comparing stored summaries today, only 82 of 259 narrowed children are byte-identical to their parent after stripping the prefix; 177 differ, and at least one child is LONGER than its parent (151 chars vs 347). So summaries evolve after creation via other write paths, and the verbatim-copy claim is established from the CREATION code, not from the current stored state. The claim that narrowing itself supplies no narrowing rests on reading that branch.

TWO CANDIDATE FIXES, EACH TESTABLE.
(a) Make narrowing narrow. The child summary should carry the specific failing statement or a concrete proposed change - the actual edit, anchored on a literal verified to occur exactly once in the deployed file - rather than the parent's prose. This is the same capability described in the separately filed gap about nothing turning a described defect into a concrete proposed change, and the two should probably be solved together.
(b) Stop resetting failed_attempts, or carry a decayed value rather than zero, so a chronically-failing gap does not return to full priority merely by acquiring a new id. This is a selection-policy change and should be measured before and after: watch whether pick cycles spent on repeatedly-failing gap families fall without starving gaps that were narrowed for good reason.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THIS ONE LOOP. The architecture expects the substrate to improve its own work queue over time. Narrowing is that mechanism. Measured over 259 attempts it returns nothing while consuming capacity in a cap-1 lane, and it actively defeats the landability filter that would otherwise stop the loop churning on gaps it cannot land.
